# v0.3.48 — A gateway message can no longer stop the application

**Upgrading from 0.3.47:**

- Rebuild and recreate the app container (`docker compose up -d --build alexclaw-prod`). No configuration or database change.
- 2FA prompts sent to Telegram or Discord now name the authenticator entry to read the code from — the TOTP issuer (`TOTP_ISSUER`, default `AlexClaw`), as the authenticator app shows it. An entry enrolled before 0.3.47 is labelled `AlexClaw` whatever `TOTP_ISSUER` says, because the variable did not reach the app until then.
- A chat locked after too many wrong codes no longer receives a 2FA prompt it cannot answer. Requesting a code while every chat is locked is refused with the time left, in the admin UI and wherever the action was started.

## Security

- **One Telegram message could restart the application — now contained.** A 2FA code sent to a chat locked after too many wrong codes crashed the Telegram gateway; the message was not acknowledged, so it came back on every restart, and four crashes in a few seconds stopped the whole application. Now:
  - a code sent to a locked chat gets a reply saying the chat (or the whole instance) is locked, and for how many minutes; the code is not checked;
  - every other result of checking a code ends in a reply, never an exception;
  - each incoming Telegram message is handled on its own: one whose handling fails is logged and acknowledged, and never delivered again;
  - the chat gateways run under their own supervisor, so a gateway that keeps crashing is restarted without stopping anything else.
- 2FA prompts name the authenticator entry, so a code is not read from the wrong one of two similar entries.
